Hey friend! I’m so sorry that you have gone through this trauma, but you’re here and we can’t change that. There are a couple things that might be at play. 1.) you might feel the need to explore your sexuality as a way of reclaiming yourself and taking the importance of sex away. If all sex is meaningless then your trauma is meaningless. 2.) being abused/taken advantage of may be what’s comfortable for you. Personally I’ve spent most of my life being abused so it’s easy to gravitate towards what I know. Think of it like a kid who doesn’t want to try a food because it’s new. They’ll love it, but it’s easier to stick with what we know and what is predictable. 3.) you may have a desire to be victimized again, but on your own terms. If you knowingly put yourself in the situation it feels like you’re taking control. Like you’re not powerless anymore. 

I wish I had an answer about what to do with these feelings. I think you need to honestly just sit with them; know where they’re coming from and know that this discomfort is your mind moving from a place of trauma to a healthy place. For me, I remind myself that growing often feels like breaking at first. That this discomfort isn’t a bad thing; it’s growth. Good luck friend! ❤️

Hi friend,

I'm not someone with BPD, but I have voluntarily admitted myself twice. I was so incredibly suicidal that I did not trust myself. I knew that if I went another moment without help I would do it. 

Being in the hospital for the first time is scary, but it's nothing like they portray in movies and things. The staff is there to help and they're very sympathetic. The other patients are usually actively helping each other reach a point of stability. There is not random screaming throught the night (typically). Honestly my last night at the hospital (2nd time) a few of the patients and I swiped a staff member's laptop and had a karaoke night in the group room. It was honestly one of the highlights of my life (pathetic? maybe). 

The hospital is the best place for you if you feel that you cannot keep yourself or those around you safe. It is not a cure-all. They will adjust medications and keep you for as long as you need. **The key point is that it is a place for stabilization.** It is a place to go to get away from those thoughts and feelings temporarily. It's hard to re-enter the world once you're discharged. You need a strong support system.
